text: At half past eight that evening, a young messenger came on a bicycle and dropped a note into the box. <break time="0.8s" /> In his answer, old Dorset wrote that our demands were a little too high. <break time="0.8s" /> If we brought Johnny home and paid him two hundred and fifty dollars, he would take the boy off our hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He also told us to come at night, because his angry neighbors might hurt anyone bringing the boy back. <break time="0.8s" /> Sam, what is two hundred and fifty dollars, after all, said Bill, One more night with this boy will drive me crazy. <break time="0.8s" /> To tell the truth, the boy had gotten on my nerves too, so I agreed. <break time="0.8s" /> We got the boy to come home by telling him that his father had bought him a silver rifle. <break time="0.8s" /> At exactly midnight we knocked at Dorsets door, and Bill counted two hundred and fifty dollars into his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> When the boy learned that we were leaving, he held Bills leg so tightly that his father had to pull him off. <break time="0.8s" /> How long can you hold him, asked Bill, and Dorset said, I think I can promise you ten minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> Enough, said Bill, and he was a mile and a half out of Summit before I caught up with him.
